key_insight: MANTRA reconstructs turbulent velocity fields from sparse, irregular measurements using continuous tensor-product representations constrained to low-rank Tucker manifolds.
engineering_relevance: The framework could extract time-resolved flow structures from sparse experimental measurements without requiring gridded observations or governing equations.
method: Represent each velocity component in a continuous tensor-product space.
Fit low-rank coefficient tensors using Riemannian optimization.
Adapt tensor rank and basis complexity to capture coordinate-wise spatiotemporal correlations.
evidence_signal: Tests on simulated isotropic turbulence and cylinder flow report reconstruction at sampling densities orders of magnitude below the underlying grids and robustness to Gaussian noise up to 20% of peak velocity; experimental jet data demonstrate evolving structure recovery.
watch_item: Performance may depend on whether the chosen tensor rank and basis complexity adequately capture the flow's multiscale structure.
paper_title: Low-Rank Tensor Manifolds for Turbulent Field Reconstruction from Sparse Data
